solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Work out cost of keeping new member of royal family

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to price something is to work out what it costs

explanation.surface: An accountant tallies what it costs to support a newborn royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a son or close male relative of a monarch, so a royal family member.

clue.text: Launches attempts to sell degrees

definitions.meaning: throws or hurls, as a ball
sales ... are attempts to persuade buyers
levels or extents, as of a slope or of excitement

explanation.surface: A firm launches its sales efforts with qualified staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Throws, sales spiels and levels of slope or intensity all share this one word.

clue.text: Suspect guerrilla's left to become resistance fighter

indicators.note: suspect means dubious, not to be trusted as it stands, so the letters are rearranged
one letter is to become another, so it is replaced

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A suspected guerrilla abandons his post to join the resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left to become resistance' means one L of the word guerrilla turns into R; 'Suspect' then signals the anagram, and only 'fighter' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier outside a regular army, such as a partisan, is a fighter of this kind.

clue.text: Language from mid-Carolina adopted by indigenous Americans

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by, so the group's name holds the piece inside

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American and First Nations people

indicators.note: mid means the central letters of the state name

explanation.surface: A language from the Carolinas taken up by Native peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed tongue that has become a native language, such as Louisiana's, is a type of language.

clue.text: Attack government protecting member with substantial appeal

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding and guarding, so the attack-plus-government pair goes around the limb

parts.note: to chin someone is informally to punch them on the chin
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A hostile assault on a government that shields one of its members, oddly with broad appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chin' as a verb (to hit on the chin) is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delightful and attractive has a great deal of appeal, which is what charming conveys.

clue.text: Broadcast tried to organise mass movement

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out over the air, so the word is as spoken

parts.note: a case is heard when it is tried in court

explanation.surface: A broadcaster attempted to coordinate a mass protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive animals together as a group is to organise them moving en masse.

clue.text: Agents infiltrating demonstration on an ethnic basis

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the agents go within the demonstration

parts.note: a rally is a mass demonstration
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of agents

explanation.surface: Spies infiltrate a protest movement organised around ethnicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with regard to race is acting on an ethnic basis, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Stupid aspect of personality a little bit curtailed

parts.note: the id is the instinctive part of the psyche in Freudian theory

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an iota is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A dim facet of someone's character, a touch reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid is used as a noun to address a fool, as in 'Listen, stupid', the same as a dunce.

clue.text: Great having positive response for article that's extremely dull

indicators.note: one thing given for another is a swap, so the article is replaced

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
yes is a positive answer

explanation.surface: A great answer in place of an article that is utterly boring.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a drab, colourless adjective means dullest of all.

clue.text: Misrepresent Greta Thunberg's principal goal

indicators.note: to misrepresent is to present wrongly, so these letters are set out in a different order
principal means first or chief, so only the opening letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction not to distort the climate activist's main aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an aim one is trying to hit, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Moan about having time to kill in rehearsal

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for moan is read backwards

parts.note: to carp is to complain or moan
to ice someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about having to fill idle time during a rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time to kill' reads as idle hours, but splits into T and ICE (slang for kill).
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a session of repeated drilling before a performance, a synonym for the answer.

clue.text: Closed urinals in need of refurbishment

indicators.note: needing to be done up, so the letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: Public toilets shut because they need refitting.
explanation.definitionFit: An island-minded, closed outlook is narrow and inward-looking.

clue.text: Auditor's welcome to settle up here

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so this signals a word as heard rather than written

parts.note: hi is a greeting or welcome
to land is to come down and settle

explanation.surface: An accountant's greeting and invitation to pay a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant and 'settle up' a bill; the auditor is a hearer, and 'up here' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Upland mountainous country lies at altitude, so a playful description of such terrain is a place up here.

clue.text: Cows Conservative post-war prime minister lacking in character

indicators.note: lacking a character means missing one letter, so a letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the British prime minister from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: A jibe that a Tory, or the post-war Labour leader, lacked personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Attlee was Britain's Labour prime minister 1945-51, famously thought colourless; 'lacking in character' looks like that jibe but means one letter (character) short.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows are bovine livestock, which the answer names collectively.

clue.text: Did volunteer take case of sweet wine?

indicators.note: taking off the case removes the outer letters

parts.note: a toffee is a chewy sweet
red is wine

explanation.surface: A volunteer asks whether he accepted a crate of dessert wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet wine' looks like one item but splits into a sweet (toffee) and red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer something is to put it forward, so the past form means put forward freely.

clue.text: Novelist let fun film spread feeling of personal achievement

parts.note: Will Self is an English novelist

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so these letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A writer allowed an entertaining movie to be released widely.
explanation.definitionFit: Realising one's own potential gives a sense of personal accomplishment, the meaning of the hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: See 15
Enlisting men wanting leadership, mounted men and men flanked by officer

indicators.note: lacking the leading letter, so the first goes
mounted means set up; in a down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

indicators.note: flanked by means with something on each side

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: Signing up recruits: foot soldiers, cavalry and men under an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing up for service, as in a course or army, is the act of enlisting.

clue.text: Extremely popular artworks stripped of aesthetic value

parts.note: cult as an adjective means hugely popular with devoted fans

indicators.note: stripped means with the outer layer removed, so first and last letters go

parts.note: murals are wall paintings, artworks

explanation.surface: Wildly fashionable art pieces deprived of real artistic merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripped of' looks like it attaches to 'aesthetic value'; 'stripped' acts alone and 'of aesthetic value' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the arts and taste, so something judged to have artistic worth.

clue.text: Cast urged actor to decrease uneven material

indicators.note: to cast is to shape or mould anew, so these letters are reformed

parts.note: read as de-crease, removing creases, which is to iron

explanation.surface: A cast member urged an actor to cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To decrease' reads as reduce, but split as de-crease it means smoothing out creases.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridged galvanised sheet metal used for roofing is a material with a wavy, uneven surface.

clue.text: Company set up suggestion boxes

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised, the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a sniff is a hint or suggestion of something

explanation.surface: A company installs suggestion boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Caskets are boxes made to hold the dead.

clue.text: See 19
Doing this up could bring a lump to one's throat

definitions.text: Doing this up could bring a lump to one's throat

parts.words: Doing this up could bring a lump to one's throat
parts.note: a lump in the throat is emotion, but literally a knot tied at the neck

explanation.surface: Something so moving that doing it would make one choke up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lump' is the knot at the collar, not emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying a cravat or similar band leaves a knot right at the throat.

clue.text: Look after English embraced by local Spanish-speaking community

indicators.note: after means the look word comes behind the rest
embraced by means held inside

parts.note: a local is a British pub, one's nearest
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: An English visitor being cared for by a Spanish-speaking village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as care for, but 'after' just places LO at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American village in the Spanish-speaking southwestern US, from Spanish for town or people.

clue.text: Position evident in half our theories

indicators.note: evident in means visible within, so the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A position that shows up in half of our theories.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming after third in a ranking is a place or position in an ordered list.

clue.text: University dons dancing nude without good reason

indicators.note: dons means puts on like clothing, so the rearranged letters wrap around the university letter
dancing means moving about, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: College academics dancing in the nude for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university lecturers but is the verb puts on: the dancing letters of nude, rearranged as UNDE, wrap round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwarranted or excessive, something happening without good reason.

clue.text: Country remains divided by Unionist halving lead

indicators.note: divided by means split by something placed in the middle

parts.note: a relic is something that remains from the past

indicators.note: halving means cutting in two, here by putting a letter between the two halves

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: A country's remnants split by a Unionist party trimming its poll lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks political (a lead in the polls) but is the metal, symbol Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: A state without a monarch, governed by elected representatives, is a kind of country.

clue.text: Image could be Apple's way to extract money from gullible people

parts.note: Apple prefixes product names with a lowercase i, as in iPhone

parts.words: way to extract money from gullible people
parts.note: a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: A cynic's view of Apple products as a scam.
explanation.definitionFit: A pictorial symbol, such as on a computer screen or a religious painting, is an image.

clue.text: About to charge to go round roundabout

indicators.note: go round means surround, so the word for charge encloses the other

parts.note: to indict is to charge formally with a crime
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to be fined for driving round a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundabout' looks like a traffic circle but is the adjective meaning circuitous.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundabout route or way of speaking is not direct, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Nine express disapproval

definitions.meaning: refers to the answer at 9 across, a goal or aim, whose synonym this is
to protest or raise a complaint

explanation.surface: Nine people protesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nine' is a cross-reference to 9 across (an aim), not a number.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is an object, and to protest against something is to object to it.

clue.text: Humming line following first half of melody in chorus

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the run goes within the word for chorus

parts.note: to sing in chorus; sing is what a chorus does

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the line letter goes after the opening fragment
takes the opening half of the word's letters

explanation.surface: Someone humming a line of melody in a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humming' suggests singing, but it is British slang for giving off a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Humming is British slang for reeking, and something reeking is giving off an odour.

clue.text: Fail, after losing one's nerve, to preserve courage

definitions.meaning: British slang for losing nerve and failing
to keep fruit in glass jars
British slang for nerve or guts

explanation.surface: Losing one's nerve and failing to keep one's courage.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for nerve, for losing it, and for preserving in jars.
